# Palanor

Palanor publishes a lattice of dated public data: U.S. and world economic series, rates, labor, prices, energy,
housing, company filings, plus Palanor's own Custom Indices and Currents. The Palanor MCP server
(`https://mcp.palanor.com`) serves it to agents. Every value comes with a `provenance` block naming its source and
licence. This skill covers when to call which tool, how to state what you found, and how to credit it.

## When to use

- The user asks about economic or market data: rates and the yield curve, jobs, inflation, growth, energy,
  housing, trade, commodities, U.S. states or other countries.
- The user asks about a Palanor Custom Index or Current, or names a palanor.com page.
- The user wants a chart or an embeddable live chart of public data, with its source.
- The user needs the source and licence of a figure they got from Palanor.

Not for single-stock, ETF, crypto or currency prices: Palanor shows those on palanor.com under a display-only
licence, and the server doesn't serve them. Not for anyone's organization data, scenarios or Palanor's Numen agent.

## Before the first call

In Goose the server's tools appear with the extension name in front: `palanor__palanor_get_signal` for
`palanor_get_signal`, and so on. The names in this skill are the server's own; add the `palanor__` prefix when
you call them.

If no `palanor__` tools are available, the extension isn't enabled. Tell the user to start Goose with the
Palanor recipe (`goose session --recipe palanor.recipe.yaml`, with `PALANOR_API_KEY` set; a free key takes a
minute at https://palanor.com/developers/keys), or to add `https://mcp.palanor.com` as a Remote Extension (Streamable HTTP) with an
`Authorization: Bearer <key>` header in `goose configure`. Never ask the user to paste a key into the chat.

## Which tool

| The user wants | Call |
|---|---|
| A series by topic ("yield curve", "Canada unemployment") | `palanor_search_signals(q="yield curve")`, then use a returned `slug` |
| To browse by category or country | `palanor_list_signals(category="labor", geo="CAN", limit=20)` |
| Where one series stands now | `palanor_get_signal(slug="rates.spread_2y10y")` |
| The latest value of several series | `palanor_get_latest(slugs=["fred_unemployment", "rates.spread_2y10y"])` |
| A series over a window | `palanor_get_observations(slug="fred_unemployment", start="2024-01-01", freq="quarter", agg="mean")` |
| Palanor's composite indices | `palanor_list_indices()`, then `palanor_get_index(slug="capital_tightness")` |
| Named macro motions (Reshoring, Remilitarization) | `palanor_list_currents()`, then `palanor_get_current(slug="remilitarization")` |
| A chart image for a post or a deck | `palanor_create_chart(signals=[{"slug": "rates.spread_2y10y"}], from="2021-01-01")`, then `palanor_get_chart(id="<job id>")` |
| A live chart on a web page | `palanor_get_embed_code(signal="rates.spread_2y10y", range="5y")` |
| A projection (Pro or Enterprise key) | `palanor_get_foresight(slug="fred_unemployment")` |

Never guess a slug. Take it from `palanor_search_signals` or `palanor_list_signals`; a guessed slug usually
returns "not found". For company filings, ownership, trackers, the release calendar and the rest, read the server's
own tool list; [references/tools.md](references/tools.md) has every argument for the tools above.

## Answering a question about a series

1. Find the slug: `palanor_search_signals(q="<the user's words>", limit=5)`. Pick the result whose `name` and `what`
   match the question. If two plausible series differ (seasonally adjusted or not, daily or monthly), say which one
   you used.
2. Read it: `palanor_get_signal(slug="<slug>")`. Use `latest_value` with `as_of`, and `context`: `percentile`
   (0 to 1, within Palanor's record since `context.since`), `record_high` / `record_low`, `highest_since` /
   `lowest_since`, `change.d30` / `d90` / `d365`, and the plain sentences in `context.read`.
3. Need a window or a trend? `palanor_get_observations(slug="<slug>", start="YYYY-MM-DD")`. Add `freq` and `agg`
   for one value per month, quarter or year. Each period carries `count`; a period with fewer readings than usual
   (a skipped release) is worth saying.
4. Answer with dates and a source line (rules below).

## Rules for what you say

1. **Every number carries its date.** Give the observation date from the data (`as_of`, `observed_at`,
   `latest.observed_at`), not the day you asked. "The 2s10s spread was 0.30 percentage points on Nov 17, 2026."
2. **Quote dated changes only.** A change needs both ends: "down 0.16 points over the 90 days to Nov 17, 2026", or
   "from 4.2% in 2025-Q2 to 4.33% in 2026-Q1". Don't write "recently", "this week" or "lately" unless you give the
   dates. `change.d90` is measured back from `as_of`, so name that end date.
3. **Percentiles and records are Palanor's record, not all of history.** Say "the highest since Feb 2011 in
   Palanor's record, which starts Jan 1990" (from `context.since`). If a field is null, it wasn't measurable; leave
   it out rather than estimate it.
4. **Monthly and quarterly series lag.** An `as_of` of the first of a month usually means that month's reading,
   published weeks later. Don't call it today's value.
5. **Revisions.** Values are as revised today. `vintage="first"` returns each observation as first published,
   where licensed; if the user asks what was known at the time, use it and say so.
6. **Projections are not data.** `palanor_get_foresight` returns a projected value with a band that holds about two
   in three outcomes. Present it as Palanor's projection with its band and its `method` line, never as a reading.
   A Free key gets an error from it; tell the user it needs a Pro or Enterprise key.

## Citing the source and licence

Every signal, observation, index and Current result has a `provenance` block:

```json
{"source": "us_treasury", "publisher": "U.S. Department of the Treasury, Bureau of the Fiscal Service",
 "license_class": "public_domain", "license_name": "Fiscal Data API license (public domain)",
 "license_url": "https://fiscaldata.treasury.gov/api-documentation/",
 "attribution": "Source: U.S. Treasury, Bureau of the Fiscal Service", "redistributable": true}
```

When you quote a value, print a source line built from it, and link the Palanor page when the result has one
(`url` or `page_url`):

> Source: U.S. Treasury, Bureau of the Fiscal Service (public domain), via Palanor
> ([palanor.com/signals/rates.spread_2y10y](https://palanor.com/signals/rates.spread_2y10y)).

- Use `provenance.attribution` as written. If it is empty, write "Source: " plus `provenance.publisher`.
- Name the licence from `license_name`, and link `license_url` when the user will republish the data.
- If `provenance.notice` is present, print it too; the source's terms require it.
- Palanor's own results (Custom Indices, Currents, Foresight) have `license_class: "palanor_derived"`: credit
  "Data: Palanor (palanor.com)" and link the methodology or Current page.
- A chart from `palanor_get_chart` returns `attribution` lines: print every line with the image.
- Several series in one answer: one source line per publisher.

More cases, and what each `license_class` allows, in [references/citing.md](references/citing.md).

## Display-only data: never present it as downloadable

Some data on palanor.com is licensed for display there and nothing else (market prices from a licensed provider,
some credit spreads, some vendor series). The server holds it back, and tells you so:

- `palanor_get_signal` or `palanor_get_observations` returns an error saying the signal is "not found, not public,
  or not licensed for redistribution";
- `palanor_get_latest` puts that error on the slug instead of a value;
- `palanor_get_embed_code` returns `embeddable: false` with a `reason`;
- a Custom Index component has `latest_value: null` and `latest_value_withheld: "licensed input: not redistributable"`.

When that happens:

- Say the series is display-only on palanor.com. Don't call it downloadable, exportable or available through the
  API, and don't offer a CSV, a chart or an embed of it.
- Don't fill in the value from memory or from another site and present it as Palanor's.
- For an index, the index value and the other components are still fine to quote. Name the withheld component,
  give its weight and say its value is withheld.
- Only a result whose `provenance.redistributable` is `true` may be passed on as data (a table, a file, a chart).

## Charts and embeds

- `palanor_create_chart` renders a checked PNG of 1 to 4 public signals. It runs asynchronously: call
  `palanor_get_chart(id="<id>")` every 10 to 15 seconds until `status` is `"done"` (usually under a minute;
  polling is free). Then give the image URL and every `attribution` line.
- Don't type numbers into `claim`. Leave it out for an automatic headline, or use tokens like `{{a.last|1}}`
  (a = the first signal). A digit typed into `claim` fails the check.
- Charts count against a monthly allowance (Free 10 a month). Make one when the user asks for an image, not to
  look at data; use `palanor_get_observations` for that.
- For a live chart on a web page, use `palanor_get_embed_code` and hand over the `iframe` as returned.

## Limits and what the server won't do

- A Free key has 1,000 requests a month. One tool call is one request, `palanor_get_latest` costs one per ten
  slugs, and chart polling is free. Prefer one `palanor_get_latest` over many `palanor_get_signal` calls when
  you only need the latest values.
- Tools marked "Requires a Pro or Enterprise key" in their description return an error on a Free key. Say what
  the user would need instead of retrying.
- The server only reads. It has no access to anyone's organization, scenarios or Palanor's Numen agent, and it
  never changes an account. Don't claim it can.

Worked examples with the exact calls: [references/examples.md](references/examples.md).
